title: Methods (AKA Functions)
description:
## Methods
Methods are reusable blocks of code. You've been using `Main` - that's a method!

```csharp
public static int Add(int a, int b)
{
    return a + b;
}
```

Breaking it down:
- `public` - accessible from anywhere (more on this later)
- `static` - belongs to the class, not an instance (more on this later)
- `int` - the return type (the function returns a value of this type)
- `Add` - the method name
- `(int a, int b)` - parameters with types
- `return` - sends a value back to the caller

### Calling a method:
```csharp
int result = Add(3, 5);
Console.WriteLine(result);  // 8
```

### Void - no return value:
```csharp
public static void Greet(string name)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Hello " + name);
}

Greet("Steve");  // Hello Steve
```

`void` means the method returns nothing. No `return` needed (though you can use `return;` to exit early).
Note that variables defined inside a function _cannot be used outside that function_
### Rules for now:
- Always use `public static` (we'll explain why later)
- Static methods can only call other static methods

---
## Assignment:
Write two methods:
- `Damage(int attack, int defense)` returns an `int`: `attack - defense` (minimum 0)
- `PrintResult(int damage)` returns `void`: prints `"Dealt <damage> damage"`

Call them in Main: calculate damage with attack=25, defense=10, then print the result.
